newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 6.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 6.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Friday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* Philippine shares are likely to trade in a narrow band with low May inflation figures discounted by the market and ahead of the next U.S. Federal Reserve meeting in early July and while waiting for the release of second quarter corporate earnings, Anscor-Hagedorn Securities analyst Russell Ong said.
* Asiamerit Securities senior analyst Ramon Saulo said the market will persist in its technical consolidation down to the 2,700 level base before bouncing back.
* On Thursday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index ended 17.67 points lower at 2,778.44.
* The Dow Jones on Wednesday ended 35.63 points higher at 7,305.29. PLDT's ADR dropped $1 to $58.
* The Philippine peso closed lower at 26.372 to the dollar vs 26.368.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average slipped to 14.03125 percent vs 16.03125.
* The National Statistics Office (NSO) reported that year-on-year inflation slowed to 4.2 percent in May compared with 4.6 percent in April, and the lowest since July 1997.
* The NSO also announced that exports in the first four months jumped 23 percent to $7.59 billion and for April alone they soared 39.6 percent to $2.08 billion from the year-ago's $1.49 billion.

* The Philippines Central Bank on Thursday cut its overnight rates by two percentage points each. Overnight borrowing rate is at 14 percent, while the lending rate is 16 percent. The Bank also lowered term reverse repo (rrp) rates by 0.375 percentage points each.

* Philippine banks would be required to set aside 30 percent of their foreign exchange assets in cash or short-term securities, Central Bank deputy governor Alberto Reyes said. The move, he said, is a prudent measure for banks to easily cover their liabilities, especially when there is a huge withdrawal of foreign currency deposits.
* Philippine reserve money in May was about 15 billion pesos below the targeted ceiling as the Central Bank maintained a prudent monetary policy, Central Bank director Diwa Gunigundo said.

* The Central Bank said the Monetary Board had relaxed its rules on bank loans for low and medium-cost homes. Loans of up to 3.5 million pesos to finance the purchase or improvement of residential units would now be excluded from the recently imposed 20 percent limit on the total a bank could lend to the property sector.
* Cash-strapped Victorias Milling Co and its creditor banks have sought another 90-day period to reach a moratorium deal, Central Bank deputy governor Alberto Reyes said.
* The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said it will issue a circular barring companies from selling shares in golf and country clubs without prior registration of the securities.
* San Miguel Brewery Hong Kong Ltd, a subsidiary of San Miguel Corp declared a HK$0.04 dividend on Thursday.

* The Philippine Senate ended its session on Thursday without passing a much-awaited comprehensive tax reform bill, essential for the country to exit from more than 30 years of supervision under the International Monetary Fund.
* Newspaper BusinessWorld reported that poultry firm Vitarich Corp may have new owners by August if negotiations with a foreign investor keen on the company are successful.
